name: Kosuke's Sloth
description: Kosuke is too lazy. He will not give you any legend, just the task: Fibonacci numbers are defined as follows: $$$f(1)=f(2)=1$$$. $$$f(n)=f(n-1)+f(n-2)$$$ $$$(3\le n)$$$ We denote $$$G(n,k)$$$ as an index of the $$$n$$$-th Fibonacci number that is divisible by $$$k$$$. For given $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$, compute $$$G(n,k)$$$. As this number can be too big, output it by modulo $$$10^9+7$$$. For example: $$$G(3,2)=9$$$ because the $$$3$$$-rd Fibonacci number that is divisible by $$$2$$$ is $$$34$$$. $$$[1,1,\textbf{2},3,5,\textbf{8},13,21,\textbf{34}]$$$.
input_specification: The first line of the input data contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. The first and only line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 10^{18}$$$, $$$1 \le k \le 10^5$$$). It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$k$$$ across all test cases does not exceed $$$10^6$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output the only number: the value $$$G(n,k)$$$ taken by modulo $$$10^9+7$$$.
approach_summary: Apply modular properties, binary exponentiation (a^b mod P in O(log b)), and modular multiplicative inverse using Extended Euclidean Algorithm.
